exact_statement: Put Phi(s,t)=(s+t)log2(s+t)-s log2(s)-t log2(t) and kappa=log2(32/27). For all real a,b,c, Phi((a+b)^2,c^2)<=Phi(a^2,c^2)+Phi(b^2,c^2)+kappa c^2, sharply at a=b=c/sqrt(8). For every disjoint Boolean substitution F=A+hD with actual Boolean uniform shadow f(z,r)=A+zD, delta=E D^2, gamma=hat h({i}), d=Inf_i(h), one has B_i(F)<=delta B_i(h)+gamma^2 B_z(f)+delta gamma^2[log2(1/gamma^2)+kappa]. The last term is <=[kappa+2/(e ln2)] Inf_i(F). This bound sums on actual represented physical stopping trees with all inherited and terminal terms retained. On any encoder-only prefix with fixed f, Q_shadow=sum_v w_v gamma_v^2 B_z(f)=B_z(f)[Var(h_root)-E Var(h_leaf)]. No universal K pays Q_shadow solely from spent encoder influence: for the quadratic-bent one-point-flip shadows on even k>=4 and a fixed balanced Maj3 encoder, every complete encoder-only policy has Q_shadow/spent_encoder_influence>=2(k-1)/3. These are interface/ownership statements, not a universal erasure-selection or FEI bound.
